rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card, impostor table and dated predictions before data; real-skeleton synthetic (six worlds; Amendment 1); replication on 4 identical-kickoff periods plus 4 natives (two kickoff-field controls, the fork week, the 04-27 reshuffle, the NE42 re-split) in two embedding models and three variants; inherited repo field from DQ4; 91 estimates rows; confirm.py frozen (SHA-256) with a dry run, not run. Missing: hour-resolution onset, holdout.
rationale.faithfulness: The onset estimators are calibrated (size 0.02; step vs slow growth separated at real counts) and agree across models in sign. But the card-level verdict is mixed: two identical weeks grow from zero, two start near full size, and the positive control is half met (#38's day-1 direction is half kept). The repo clause hits one week's first day. Day resolution cannot separate a fast instability from a field. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F2 G1 H1 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A caution for operators: the first day's room difference is a poor guide to the week, and inherited work rarely sets it. No lever and no effect size to act on.

one_line: The #best/#rest content split has no single onset shape: it grows from zero in #37 and #39, is nearly full on day 1 in #41 and #42 with a half-kept direction, and inherited repos set it only on #42's first day.
